title.narrative: UNEP Copenhagen Climate Center

description.narrative:
To contribute to the combined Danish and UNEP priorities of achieving SDG7 targets 7.1 and 7.3 – ensure universal access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all and double the global rate of improvement in energy efficiency as well as SDG13 - urgent action to combat climate change and its impact by 2030.
Denmark has supported the development and competencies of the UNEP DTU Partnership for more than 30 years. It has become a trusted partner to the UNFCCC, international donors and developing countries by delivering high quality research, knowledge products, technical assistance and other services. The UNEP DTU Partnership is recognised as a Centre of Excellence within the fields of renewable energy, energy efficiency and climate change, and will during the cost-extension/bridging period be turned into the UNEP-CCC.

title.narrative: Identified opportunities and developed concept proposals for bundled/aggregated investment projects through direct engagements with countries (at national and subnational levels).

target.value: Increasing evidence of information sharing between engaged governments leading to endogenous replication of project approaches.

actual.value: C2E2 has implemented EE in buildings in 10 municipalities in Chile, implemented EE lighting in schools in Kenya, and has had a further focus on African countries in support of UNEP efforts and promotion by using C2E2 tools.

title.narrative: Strengthen local vocational skills in the area of energy efficiency.
Energy efficiency skills network scoped and established with key partners; progress of rollout of capacity building activities.

target.value: Global impact through progress on implementation building on efforts in previous years.

actual.value: C2E2 has trained trainers in Sri Lanka on EE in transport, trainers in Kenya on EE in manufacturing and the commercial sector, and has designed the master program on EE in manufacturin-commercial sector in Kenya and the master in EE in Road Transport in Sri Lanka.

title.narrative: Outcome 3: Within Centre on Energy, Climate and Sustainable Development: High quality annual adaptation and emissions gap reports are made available to the international climate community and considered in negotiations

Recognition by leading climate change stakeholders of the importance and relevance of the reports assessed through surveys. References to Gap reports in media, literature, etc. captured in UN Environment media reports. Evidence for submission of more ambitious NDCs to the UNFCCC.

Develop a strong, growing and widely used KMS and learning support program including best practices, innovative business models and delivery mechanisms leading to engagement with countries and cities.

Reported and measurable increase in use and function of the Knowledge Management System including through number of records/number of unique visitors, and reported and measurable increase in reach of e-learning activities documented by number of webinars held/participant attendance levels.

target.value: Increase in number of KMS records/unique visitors and webinars/number of participants.

actual.value: No data on number og KMS records / unique visitors, yet C2E2 har delivered various outputs to strengthen a KMS, including one report on the regulatory barriers for ESCO development, a guidebook on EE and sustainable transport in medium-sized municipalities, a brief on cities' best practices on energy efficiency.
